function_question: How does nature collect water from the air?

opening.text: There was a boy called Omar who looked after his school garden on a dry hillside where it hardly ever rains.
Thick fog rolled in every morning and wrapped the garden in mist, but the plants stayed thirsty and droopy.
Omar looked at the fog and wondered: "There's water all around us. What if we could catch it for the garden?"

card.place: A garden on a dry hillside
card.rules: Mesh, string, plastic, straws, a cup

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Water in the fog
chapters.line: Omar wonders: what if we could catch the fog for the garden?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Omar needs a teammate
chapters.line: Catching fog is a two-person job. Will you join Omar?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Omar meet desert heroes who drink from thin air.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the fog
chapters.line: The heroes share how tiny droplets become a drink.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training in the steam lab
chapters.line: With an adult's help, Omar hangs three materials over the steam.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The why hunt
chapters.line: You keep asking why, until you reach the real problem.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great fog catcher starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The big mist test
chapters.line: The drops miss the cup. You fix it, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: The garden turns green
chapters.line: Every morning the fog waters the garden, drop by drop.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Omar's garden gets fog every morning but almost no rain. Can you help him turn the mist into water? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea for catching water from the air. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been drinking fog for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who catch water from the air!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which material will catch the most water from the steam? Ask an adult to help with the hot water.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your fog catcher like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your fog catcher, then mist it with a spray bottle from 1 metre away. How much water reaches the cup?
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change the mesh or the angle, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, YOUR fog catcher waters Omar's school garden every morning, and the whole hillside is green!

quick_check.question: Omar's catcher collects 20 millilitres every 10 minutes. How much does it collect in 30 minutes?
quick_check.right: Right! 20 + 20 + 20 = 60 millilitres. Imagine how much a whole morning of fog could give!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. 30 minutes is three lots of 10 minutes.

clue_cards.name: Namib desert beetle
clue_cards.trick: It does a headstand into the fog, with water-loving bumps on its back.
clue_cards.does: The bumps catch droplets, which grow and roll down waxy grooves into its mouth.

clue_cards.name: Thorny devil
clue_cards.trick: Tiny channels run between its scales.
clue_cards.does: They pull water from damp sand across its skin to its mouth.

clue_cards.name: Spider silk
clue_cards.trick: Each thread has little knots along it.
clue_cards.does: Fog droplets collect on the knots and grow into big, sparkly drops.

clue_cards.name: Cactus
clue_cards.trick: Its spines are cone-shaped with tiny grooves.
clue_cards.does: Fog collects on the tips and slides down to the plant's base.

predict.prompt: Floats in the air or falls down? Predict first!

items.label: Lots of droplets joined on a net

predict.explain: Fog droplets are too tiny to fall. When they hit something and join up, they get heavy enough to roll away down a smooth path.

lab.title: The steam lab
lab.predict: Hang each material in the steam for 5 minutes. Which one will drip the most water into its cup?

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: 5 Whys is like being a detective. You ask "why?" again and again, each time digging one level deeper, until you find the real cause of a problem. Today you'll learn the first 3 whys.

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 🚌 Why was the bus late? It got stuck in traffic.
parts.starter: Why is the garden dying? Because…

parts.name: Why #2
parts.what: Take that answer and ask why again.
parts.example: 🚌 Why was there traffic? A road was closed.
parts.starter: Why are the plants so thirsty? Because…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 🚌 Why was the road closed? Workers were fixing a pipe.
parts.starter: Why doesn't the fog's water reach the roots? Because…

sketch_checklist: I drew my fog catcher from the front and the side.
I showed where the droplets stick and which way they run.
I showed how the water gets into the cup.

test.check_question: Does the water reach the cup, or drip off somewhere else?

reflection.question: Which nature hero did your fog catcher copy?
